rationale.text: The test applies only to decorative images without a caption, and code cannot tell which images those are. The glossary defines a decorative image as one with no function and no particular information relative to the content it goes with, and the caption glossary adds that an image whose adjacent text can stand in for it may be treated as decorative. Whether an image has a caption is partly judgment too: the caption glossary covers adjacent text that informs on the image, not only figure and figcaption. So no check can fault an element as surely in scope, nor pass a page, and the entry stays at none, although each condition of the test is mechanical once an element is known to be in scope. The wording says "ces conditions", and the methodology checks them together before "le test est validé", so each condition is its own requirement with one route. The caption limit is an exception on each, from the wording and technical note 1. Whether content between the tags acts as a text alternative may itself need judgment. No axe rule is tagged, and no custom check is registered: a hint check on canvas elements with aria-hidden="true" that still carry an alternative would be evidence only, and could be added later. Applicability is judgment. Needs is empty.
